text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The edit matches the ticket and the actual code. best_route, sites_served, and trips_needed are preserved unchanged; can_pass is imported from logistics.access with the correct signature (road_id, vehicle, network). passable_route loads the network the same way best_route does, filters routes usable by truck or van via can_pass over route['roads'], picks min by (km, id) like best_route, returns (route, 'truck') only if a truck can use every road else (route, 'van'), and None when nothing is usable. rerouted_sites derives warehouses from distinct r['from'] values, unions sites via the existing sites_served helper, and includes a site only when both best_route and passable_route return results with different route ids (vehicle-only changes excluded), sorted in name order. Checked against data/network.json: SITE-CPL-B reroutes RT-05→RT-06 (R-08 closed, R-09 restricted→van), SITE-HGL-A reroutes RT-07→RT-08 (R-12 closed), while SITE-NVL-B and SITE-HGL-B keep their routes with a van — consistent with the ticket's semantics."}}
reasoning:
Check the proposed edit against the code.

passable_route: loads network, gets routes, filters usable by truck or van, picks min by (km, id), returns truck if truck can use all roads else van. Matches ticket.

rerouted_sites: warehouses from distinct r["from"], sites via sites_served, for each site picks warehouse = next(w for w in warehouses if site in sites_served(w, network)). Each site is served by exactly one warehouse in this data. best_route and passable_route compared by route id. Sorted output. Matches ticket.

One subtlety: `network = network or load_network()` — fine, consistent with existing code.

can_pass signature: can_pass(road, vehicle, network) — proposed _usable_by calls can_pass(road, vehicle, network) — matches.

Edge: passable_route returns None if no usable route; rerouted_sites handles that. Ticket says "if passable_route returns None the site is not rerouted" — handled by `best and passable`.

Check best_route unchanged — yes, identical.

sites_served and trips_needed preserved.

One thing: rerouted_sites uses `next(w for w in warehouses if site in sites_served(w, network))` — could raise StopIteration if a site isn't served by any warehouse, but sites are derived from sites_served, so fine.

Also check: does the ticket say passable_route should send a truck if a truck may use every road on that route and a van otherwise — yes, implemented.

Verify semantics with data: SITE-NVL-B: best_route picks RT-02 (22km, roads R-01 A, R-03 R) — truck can't use R-03, van can. passable_route: RT-02 usable by van, RT-03 usable by truck/van. Usable routes: both. min by km: RT-02 (22). Truck can't use all roads → van. Route same as best_route → not rerouted. Hmm, but ticket says "the vehicle alone changing does not count" — correct, RT-02 same id, so not included. Good.

SITE-CPL-B: best RT-05 (18km, R-07 A, R-08 X) — unusable. RT-06 (R-07 A, R-09 R) usable by van. passable → (RT-06, "van"). Different id → rerouted. Good.

SITE-HGL-A: best RT-07 (20km, R-10 A, R-12 X) unusable. RT-08 usable. Rerouted. Good.

SITE-HGL-B: RT-09, R-13 R — van only. passable → (RT-09, "van"), same route id → not rerouted. Good.

Everything checks out. Accept.
